subject: Contract cycle cutover — notice mechanics and termination-for-convenience alignment
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@nusystems.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Contract cycle cutover — notice mechanics and termination-for-convenience alignment

Jorge — thanks again for the time yesterday. As we prepare the order form + MSA redlines for NúSystems, two quick coordination asks so we can keep the timeline for a late-May go-live:

1) Notice window for non-renewal / cancel: NúSystems asked for a 90-day opt-out notice for the annual term. Our standard is 60 days (and some pilots are 30). Can you confirm whether the 90 is firm? If so, we need to align on what constitutes valid notice (email to procurement + account owner vs signed form).

2) Termination for convenience: you asked for a right to terminate for convenience at any time with pro-rated refund. We can do a limited T4C with 30 days' notice and a short-tail phase-out for consumed credits. We cannot accept immediate termination + refund for used compute credits.

I've attached a focused redline (NIM-OF-v3_redline.pdf) that:
- Marks the switch from 60 -> 90 days as a tracked change (Section 2.1)
- Adds a short T4C appendix proposing 30 days' notice and a usage reconciliation table

Laura — would you please review the T4C appendix and call out any language that would jeopardize our ability to preserve cached models / reserved capacity obligations? Hannah, if NúSystems insists on 90 days, we should confirm pricing implications (committed capacity sizing) before committing.

Next steps: Jorge, can you confirm by end of day Friday whether 90 days is a hard requirement and whether procurement needs a specific notice format? If yes, we will iterate the redline this week.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
A: +1 (415) 555-0137

Attachments: NIM-OF-v3_redline.pdf (PDF, 42 KB)

From: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@nusystems.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nusystems.com, NúSystems Legal <legal@nusystems.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Contract cycle cutover — notice mechanics and termination-for-convenience alignment

Kimberly — thanks for the quick follow up. Short answers from procurement: we prefer a 90-day notice for multi-year contracts (risk window for budget forecasts), but we're open to a 60 → 90 tiered approach tied to TCV thresholds.

Regarding format: procurement will accept an email to procurement@nusystems.com with the signed order form as evidence of notice (we can do a DocuSign anchor).

On T4C: finance expects a pro-rated refund for any pre-paid, unused committed capacity, but legal flagged that we should provide a reconciliation window (30–45 days) to sort invoices/cutover. We'll review your redline and send consolidated comments by Friday.

-Jorge

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Contract cycle cutover — notice mechanics and termination-for-convenience alignment

Kim / Hannah — flagged a few legal concerns after a first pass on the T4C appendix in the attached spreadsheet (redwood-termination-comparison.xlsx). High level: 

- We can agree to 30 days' notice for T4C (commercial compromise) but must require a reconciliation period of 45 days after termination for consumption / KV-cache eviction costs and final billing.
- The language must exempt force majeure and termination for cause; otherwise they could claim termination for convenience to escape performance obligations.
- For auto-renew: we should preserve a clear reminder cadence (two notifications: 90 days + 30 days) and require express opt-out via signed e-form or email to procurement@nusystems.com.

I've suggested concrete clause language in the spreadsheet on rows 12–24. I'll convert to tracked changes in the OF redline if you want to send a second draft to NubSystems legal.

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@nusystems.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Contract cycle cutover — notice mechanics and termination-for-convenience alignment

Jorge — appreciate the context. Two updates based on internal legal/finance: 

1) T4C: we're prepared to accept a 30-day termination-for-convenience with a 45-day reconciliation window. During the reconciliation window, Redwood will: (a) cease provisioning new reserved capacity within 7 days, (b) run final usage reconciliation, and (c) return any unused pre-paid portion per the reconciliation. We cannot refund consumption that occurred prior to the termination notice.

2) Auto-renew notice cadence: we'll include two reminders — notification at 90 days and a final reminder at 30 days. Notice must be sent to procurement@nusystems.com and the account owner; opt-out requires a signed email or DocuSign acknowledgement.

Attached is a revised OF with tracked changes that implements the two items above. If NúSystems agrees to this approach, we can lock pricing and schedule a DocuSign send next week.

Next: Laura, please confirm whether the proposed "cease provisioning new reserved capacity within 7 days" language exposes us operationally. Marcus, any capacity or billing impacts we should highlight to Jorge?

Thanks,
Kim

Attachments: NIM-OF-v3_redline.pdf (updated, 56 KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@nusystems.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Contract cycle cutover — notice mechanics and termination-for-convenience alignment

Kim / Jorge — operational note from capacity and billing: the proposed 7-day cease-to-provision triggers a few items for ops:

- We need a confirmed list of reserved instances tied to the order form so we can mark them for drift/retirement. Please include the committed pool IDs in the final OF.
- A 45-day reconciliation is doable but engineering will require a full access window to logs and usage counters to validate final consumption. Expect a one-time reconciliation invoice adjustment line (positive or negative).
- If NúSystems has pinned model variants in our dedicated pool, we can provide a controlled warm-down plan (eviction schedule) to minimize cold-start P99 spikes for any dependent applications. That plan adds ~1–2 business days to the reconciliation timeline.

If the customer accepts the proposed approach, ops and billing will put the reconciliation flow in the SOW appendix and provide an estimated refund range within 3 business days of final usage calc.

—Marcus
Director, Dedicated Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@nusystems.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:48:00 -0500
Subject: RE: Contract cycle cutover — notice mechanics and termination-for-convenience alignment

Team — thanks for the clarity. NúSystems is comfortable with the 30-day T4C + 45-day reconciliation. A couple of small asks before DocuSign: 

1) Please add an explicit example in the SOW appendix showing the reconciliation math (committed credits — consumed credits = refund).
2) For the auto-renew reminders, procurement wants the reminders to be sent to two addresses: procurement@nusystems.com and budget-ops@nusystems.com.

We reviewed the redline and will sign off after the two small edits. Expect a DocuSign request by EOD Thursday once you confirm the two items.

-Jorge
